MUQATIL:79:34-41/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r4.claim: Jesus's peace at birth refers to his first creation without a father, at death to the grave's pressure, and at resurrection to his proof against those who called him Lord.
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r4.anchor: والسلام علي يوم ولدت يعنيفي الخلق الأولى من غير أب

STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r11.claim: Zachariah and Mary’s temporary silences are paired with the infant Jesus’ miraculous speech.
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r11.anchor: Zachariah and Mary’s temporary silence (vv. 10–11, 26) is complemented

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r2.claim: Peace protects Jesus from Satan’s touch at birth, the hardships of death, and the terror of resurrection and Hell; the same protection came to John.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r2.anchor: بلا والد طبيعي أي : من طعن الشيطان

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r3.claim: The definite peace may mean peace in full, while asserting peace for himself implicitly curses his enemies; the phrase in 20:47 likewise implies punishment for deniers.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r3.anchor: فإن إثبات جنس السلام لنفسه تعريض لإثبات ضده لأضداده

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r4.claim: After Jesus spoke, people knew Mary was chaste and innocent; he did not speak again until the usual age of speech.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r4.anchor: أيقنوا ببراءة أمه وأنها من أهل العصمة والبعد من الريبة

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r5.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r5.claim: An objection reads the resurrection phrase as proof that there is no life in the grave; the answer is that it means everlasting resurrection life, unlike the grave’s life.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r5.anchor: يدل على أن لا حياة في القبر لأنه ذكر حياة واحدة

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r6.claim: Barzakh life is intermediate: it is life of the spirit alone, while resurrection life joins spirit and body; spirits do not cease living after their creation.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r6.anchor: حياة البرزخ على النصف من حياة يوم البعث فإن الأولى حياة الروح فقط

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r7.claim: John’s peace is indefinite and Jesus’ definite because a little from God is much; Hasan’s reading of guide us to a straight path signals contentment with little.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r7.anchor: ثم إنه نكر في سلام يحيى وعرف في سلام عيسى لأن الأول من الله

BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r8.speaker: الشيخ
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r8.claim: The sheikh explains that John’s third-person wording differs from Jesus’ first-person wording and says both possess the realities of annihilation and completeness.
BURSEVI:v5p254#4/r8.anchor: قال شيخي وسندي في "كتاب البرقيات" له قدس سره إنما أتى بطريق الغيبة

BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r1.claim: A report says John warned Jesus against feeling secure from God’s plan, while Jesus warned John against despairing of mercy; God loves the one with the better expectation of Him.
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r1.anchor: أوحى الله تعالى إليهما أن أحبكما إلي أحسنكما ظنا بي

BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r2.claim: John’s blood continued boiling until seventy thousand were killed in retaliation, while Jesus was raised to the highest heaven, manifesting beauty; each attained perfection in his station.
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r2.anchor: فلم يزل فائرا دمه حتى قتل من أجله سبعون ألفا قصاصا منه

BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r3.claim: Inwardly Jesus represents meaning born from divine breath in the heart, which can die under overpowering ego traits and practices; even the spiritually alive should not presume immunity.
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r3.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" قوله : {ويوم أموت} فيه إشارة إلى أن عيسى المعنى المتولد

BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r4.speaker: التكملة
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r4.claim: The account dates Jesus’ birth to the Successor kings, says Mary was thirteen, Jesus received prophethood at thirty and was raised at thirty-three, and Mary lived six years afterward.
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r4.anchor: وكان حمل مريم به وهي ابنة ثلاث عشرة سنة ونبىء عيسى وهو ابن ثلاثين سنة

BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r5.speaker: التكملة
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r5.claim: Mary took the young Jesus to Egypt with Joseph the carpenter to escape Herod; Persian envoys arrived because of a star and were warned by an angel not to tell Herod.
BURSEVI:v5p255#2/r5.anchor: وأمر الله مريم أن ينتقل به إلى مصر ومعهما يوسف بن يعقوب النجار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r1.claim: Al-salām is generic peace, implicitly cursing Mary's accusers: if all peace is assigned to Jesus, its opposite is being wished on his enemies. The apparent reading as a definite, previously mentioned peace is unlikely and misses the polemical insinuation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r1.anchor: والأظهر بل الصحيح أن التغريب للجنس جيء به تعريضا باللعنة على متهمي مريم وأعدائها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r2.claim: The comparison ‘peace upon the one who follows guidance’ means punishment for the one who denies and turns away (20:47); the context is one of dispute and hostility.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r2.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى ( والسلام على من اتبع الهدى ) يعني أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r3.claim: Identifying an antecedent from John’s peace fails because the passage is separate in narrative and sense; assigning peace by generic usage better creates the contrast required by the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r3.anchor: لأن هذا الكلام منقطع عن ذلك وجودا وسدرا فيكون معهودا غير سابق لفظا ومعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r4.claim: One view makes John's greeting stronger because God spoke it; another makes Jesus' stronger because God places Jesus in His own position and gives him exclusive peace, a comparison left for reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r4.anchor: وقيل هذا أرجح لما فيه من إقامة الله تعالى إياه في ذلك مقام نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r5.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī reads waladtu with feminine tāʾ, making the verb agree with Jesus' mother.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p90#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( يوم ولدت ) بتاء التأنيث وإسناد الفعل إلى والدته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.claim: Peace at birth means safety from Satan's piercing, at death from shirk, and at resurrection from terrors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.anchor: أي عند الموت من الشرك، {ويوم أبعث حيا} من الأهوال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.claim: Jesus's speech made the people recognize Mary's innocence; he then remained silent until children normally begin speaking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.anchor: ثم سكت عيسى عليه السلام، فلم يتكلم بعد ذلك حتى بلغ المدة التي يتكلم فيها الصبيان

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:33-34/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:33-34/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:33-34/r1.claim: Jesus' peace parallels Yahya's; the article is either referential or generic. Calling peace on himself insinuates a curse on his enemies, as the wording “peace on whoever follows guidance” implies punishment for deniers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:33-34/r1.anchor: والتعريف للعهد والأظهر أنه للجنس والتعريض باللعن على أعدائه

QASHANI:19:33-35/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:33-35/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:33-35/r1.claim: Jesus shares Yahya's peace in three stations because his essence is abstract and sanctified, unhidden by matter even in childhood.
QASHANI:19:33-35/r1.anchor: { والسلام علي } في المواطن الثلاثة كما على يحيى لكون ذاتي مجردة مقدسة لا تحتجب بالمواد

QASHANI:19:33-35/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:33-35/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:33-35/r2.claim: Peace means freedom from defects that arise through attachment to matter.
QASHANI:19:33-35/r2.anchor: إذ معنى السلام: التنزه عن العيوب اللاحقة بواسطة تعلق المادة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r15.claim: Peace protects Jesus at birth, death, and resurrection; being born and resurrected shows his humanity, while his birth was not harmed by Satan.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r16.claim: The peace is glad tidings for believers and a warning to those who deny Jesus, whose enemies thereby incur a curse.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r16.anchor: فهو بشارة لمن صدقة فإنه منه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r17.claim: The Prophet was not given the infant-speech sign lest his people confuse him with soothsayers; infant, animal, and inanimate speech are other wonders.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p531/r17.anchor: ولم يكن لنبينا صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم مثل هذه الخارقة

DURR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.claim: Mujahid reports Mary said Jesus spoke to her alone but glorified God in her womb when she was with people.
DURR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: قالت مريم: كنت إذا خلوت حدثني عيسى وكلمني وهو في بطني

DURR-FULL:v5p509/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p509/r10.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v5p509/r10.claim: The three moments of human frailty are birth, death, and resurrection, the moments Jesus names in his greeting of peace.
DURR-FULL:v5p509/r10.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: فقرات ابن آدم ثلاث: يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث

QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r1.claim: Jesus says peace upon himself, unlike the Prophet's greeting during the Night Journey, and peace means safety.
QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r1.anchor: قال عيسى عليه السلام : { والسلام على } وقال لنبينا عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p240/r2.claim: Jesus is safe at birth from Christians' excessive praise and Jews' disparagement, and safe at death and resurrection from trials outside divine union.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r8.claim: Birth, death, and resurrection are singled out as moments when a person especially needs God's mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r8.anchor: وذكر المواطن التي خصها لأنها أوقات حاجة الإنسان إلى رحمة الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r9.speaker: مالك بن أنس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r9.claim: Malik says the verse is difficult for adherents of predestination: Jesus states his decreed course through death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p15/r9.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس رضي الله عنه في هذه الآية: ما أشدها على أهل القدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r1.claim: The salām is God's protection of Jesus from Satan's harm on the day he was born; the earlier explanation is at 19:15.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون السلامة علي من الله يوم ولدت حتى لم يضرني شيطان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r2.claim: One explanation for al-salām with the definite article is that it echoes the prior mention of salām without the article, though the speakers differ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r2.anchor: لما جرى ذكر السلام قبل هذا الموضع بغير ألف ولام كان الأحسن أن يرد ثانية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r3.claim: He answers the objection by saying Jesus may have learned God's wording about Yaḥya and applied it to himself; alternatively, God changed the quoted wording naturally, as speakers may paraphrase.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r3.anchor: عيسى إنما يتعلم من ربه فيجوز أن يكون سمع قول الله في يحيى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r4.claim: A second answer is that salāmun and al-salāmu are dialectal forms with the same meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p230#2/r4.anchor: أن سلاما والسلام لغتان بمعنى واحد ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p230/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p230/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p230/r1.claim: Jesus' greeting of peace at birth, death, and resurrection affirms that he is God's created servant who lives, dies, and is raised like other creatures, while protected in these hardest moments.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p230/r1.anchor: وأنه مخلوق من خلق الله يحيا (2) ويموت ويبعث كسائر الخلائق

FARRA:v2p167/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p167/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p167/r4.claim: The transmitted interpretation of al-salām ʿalayya is ‘safety be upon me.’
FARRA:v2p167/r4.anchor: وقوله: والسلام علي [33] جاء في التفسير السلامة علي.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r14.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r14.claim: Peace means safety in worldly life, the grave, and resurrection, covering Jesus' three states; this is al-Kalbi's view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r14.anchor: يعني بالاسلام السلامة , يعني في الدنيا , { ويوم أموت } يعني في القبر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r15.claim: Another view gives protection from Satan's poke at birth and grave pressure because Jesus was not buried; the author finds the resurrection reading unsatisfactory but suggests safety from reckoning because God raised him after clearing him of sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r15.anchor: ليس مولود يولد إلا همزه الشيطان وذلك حين يستهل , غير عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jesus' speech stopped until he reached boyhood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p370/r16.anchor: قال ابن عباس ثم انقطع كلامه حتى بلغ مبلغ الغلمان

MUQATIL:19:33/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:33/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:33/r1.claim: When Jesus said he was dutiful to his mother but named no father, Zechariah embraced him and testified that he was God's servant and messenger.
MUQATIL:19:33/r1.anchor: فلما ذكر الوالدة، ولم يذكر الوالد، ضمه زكريا إلى صدره، وقال: أشهد أنك عبد الله ورسوله،

MUQATIL:19:33/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:33/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:33/r2.claim: Jesus' greeting of peace at birth, death, and resurrection refers to those times, including his being raised alive after death in the Hereafter; he then stopped speaking and grew like other children.
MUQATIL:19:33/r2.anchor: يعني حين ولدت، { ويوم أموت } ، يعني وحين أموت، { ويوم أبعث حيا } [آية: 33]

NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r1.claim: The three days are temporal adverbials governed by the predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r1.anchor: يوم ظرف والعامل فيه الخبر وهو على

NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r2.claim: If the definite article refers back to Yahya's peace, the same peace at birth, death, and resurrection is directed to Jesus.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r2.anchor: أي ذلك السلام الموجه إلى يحيى في المواطن الثلاثة موجه إلى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r3.claim: If the article is generic, the verse means that peace as a kind rests upon Jesus and indirectly implies a curse on Mary's opponents in this dispute.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p36#3/r3.anchor: وان كان للجنس فالمعنى وجنس السلام على وفيه تعريض باللعنه على أعداء مريم وابنها

QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r4.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the second occurrence of al-salam has the definite article because the earlier one lacked it.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r4.anchor: ذكر السلام قبل هذا بغير ألف ولام فحسن في الثانية ذكر الألف واللام

QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r5.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the three greetings as peace for Jesus in worldly life, the grave, and resurrection, his three states of being alive, dead, and raised.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r5.anchor: لأن له أحوالا ثلاثة: في الدنيا حيا، وفي القبر ميتا، وفي الآخرة مبعوثا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r6.claim: The birth greeting can alternatively mean protection from Satan’s whispering, as discussed under Aal Imran; Jesus then stopped speaking in the cradle until boyhood.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r6.anchor: وقيل: من همز الشيطان كما تقدم في «آل عمران

QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r7.claim: Qatada recounts a woman telling Jesus that his womb and nursing mother were blessed; Jesus replied that those who read, follow, and practice God’s Book are blessed.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:33/r7.anchor: طوبى للبطن الذي حملك، والثدي الذي أرضعك

RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r1.claim: Some take the article in “the peace” as referring to the peace previously given to John.
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r1.anchor: لام التعريف في السلام منصرف إلى ما تقدم في قصتي يحيى

RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers the article as comprehensive: claiming all peace for Jesus and his followers leaves only a curse for Mary’s accusers, an insinuation suited to the hostile context.
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r2.anchor: الصحيح أن يكون هذا التعريف تعويضا باللعن على من اتهم مريم

RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r3.claim: A report has Jesus tell John that John is better because God gave him peace while Jesus gave peace to himself; al-Hasan answers that God’s greeting to Jesus is his own greeting.
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r3.anchor: روى بعضهم عن عيسى عليه السلام أنه قال ليحيى أنت خير مني سلم الله عليك

RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r4.claim: Al-Qadi explains peace as safety from harms and afflictions; Jesus asks for the safety granted to John at the three most vulnerable moments: birth, death, and resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v21p184/r4.anchor: السلام عبارة عما يحصل به الأمان ومنه السلامة في النعم وزوال الآفات

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.claim: Peace at John’s birth means protection from Satan; at death, exemption from grave trials.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.anchor: protection for him against the evil promptings of Satan (R, Ṭ); the blessing upon him the day he dies indicates that he is exempt from the trials of the grave

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r122.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r122.speaker: R, Q
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r122.claim: Jesus’ infant speech may have been temporary; after speaking, he returned to ordinary infant incapacity.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r122.anchor: after delivering the statements recounted in vv. 30–33 Jesus returned to the ordinary state of an infant

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r139.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r139.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r139.claim: Jesus’ threefold peace parallels John’s and means Satan did not touch him at birth.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r139.anchor: he was spared Satan’s touch on the day he was born (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r140.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r140.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r140.claim: Jesus will be free from fear at death after his return and at resurrection with humanity.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r140.anchor: he will be free from fear on the day he dies (after his return to earth

NAHHAS:v3p16/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p16/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p16/r3.claim: This ends Jesus's speech; his speaking in his mother's lap manifested the sign.
NAHHAS:v3p16/r3.anchor: آخر كلام عيسى عليه السلام فلما تكلم في حجر أمه

TAB-FULL:v15p534/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p534/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p534/r1.claim: Peace means God's protection from Satan at birth, from the terror of death, and from the fear of the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v15p534/r1.anchor: يقول: والأمنة من الله علي من الشيطان وجنده يوم ولدت أن ينالوا مني ما ينالون ممن يولد عند الولادة،

TAB-FULL:v15p534/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p534/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p534/r2.claim: Wahb says Jesus' words tell people that he had no father, would die, and would be raised alive.
TAB-FULL:v15p534/r2.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، {والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا} [مريم: 33] قال: يخبرهم في قصة خبره عن نفسه، أنه لا أب له وأنه سيموت ثم يبعث حيا،

TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.claim: The wording change for birth, death, and resurrection portrays the greeting of peace as applying during Jesus's lifetime.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.anchor: لتمثيل أن التسليم في حال حياته عليه السلام

TABATABAI:19:15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r6.speaker: علي موسى الرضا
TABATABAI:19:15/r6.claim: Al-Riḍa says the most frightening moments are birth, death, and resurrection; God granted John peace at all three, as Jesus also proclaimed peace over himself at those stages.
TABATABAI:19:15/r6.anchor: قال سمعت أبا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام يقول إن أوحش ما يكون هذا الخلق

TABATABAI:19:31-36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r6.claim: Jesus invokes peace upon himself at the three comprehensive turning points of his existence: birth, death, and resurrection.
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r6.anchor: تسليم منه على نفسه في المواطن الثلاثة الكلية التي تستقبله في كونه ووجوده

TABATABAI:19:31-36/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r7.claim: Unlike the indefinite peace in Yahya’s story, Jesus’s definite expression signifies comprehensive peace; God gives peace to Yahya, while Jesus gives it to himself.
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r7.anchor: السلام في قصة يحيى نكرة يدل على النوع، وفي هذه القصة محلى بلام الجنس يفيد بإطلاقه الاستغراق

TABATABAI:19:31-36/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r8.claim: The one who grants peace to Yahya is God, whereas Jesus grants it to himself.
TABATABAI:19:31-36/r8.anchor: وهو أن المسلم على يحيى هو الله سبحانه وعلى عيسى هو نفسه

TABRISI:19:31-33/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:31-33/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:31-33/r10.claim: Salām is a verbal noun of salima, and is also one of God's names.
TABRISI:19:31-33/r10.anchor: السلام مصدر سلمت والسلام جمع سلامة والسلام اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

TABRISI:19:31-33/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:31-33/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:31-33/r11.claim: Indefinite salām may begin a sentence because this greeting is frequently used and generic nouns often occur initially.
TABRISI:19:31-33/r11.anchor: وسلام مما يبتدأ به في النكرة لأنه اسم يكثر استعماله

TABRISI:19:31-33/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:31-33/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:31-33/r12.claim: Since salām appeared earlier without the article, repeating it here with the article is stylistically preferable.
TABRISI:19:31-33/r12.anchor: لما جرى ذكر سلام قبل هذا الموضع بغير ألف ولام كان الأحسن أن يرد ثانية

TABRISI:19:31-33/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:31-33/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:31-33/r19.claim: God's safety is with Jesus at birth, death, and resurrection, as explained earlier in the account of John.

TABRISI:19:31-33/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:31-33/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:31-33/r20.claim: A person may describe praiseworthy qualities to inform others, provided he is not boasting.
TABRISI:19:31-33/r20.anchor: يجوز أن يصف الإنسان نفسه بصفات المدح إذا أراد تعريفها إلى غيره لا على وجه الافتخار

TABRISI:19:31-33/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:31-33/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:31-33/r21.claim: One report says Jesus's words established Mary's innocence; he then remained silent until children ordinarily begin speaking.
TABRISI:19:31-33/r21.anchor: قيل: ولما كلمهم عيسى ع بهذا علموا براءة مريم

THALABI:v6p214#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p214#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p214#2/r9.claim: Jesus’ greeting of peace covers his birth, death, and being raised alive.
THALABI:v6p214#2/r9.anchor: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r1.claim: The definite article in السلام is more fitting because the preceding mention used indefinite سلام; here it means complete safety.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r1.anchor: لما جرى ذكر السلام قبل هذا بغير ألف ولام كان الأحسن أن يذكر ثانية بالألف واللام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r2.claim: They understand God's protection at Jesus's birth to include freedom from Satan's touch; a prophetic report says Satan touches each newborn except Jesus, where the barrier intervened.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r2.anchor: السلامة علي من الله تعالى يوم ولدت حتى لم يضرني شيطان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r3.claim: The verse repeats the account of peace given for Yahya earlier in this surah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r3.anchor: والآية مفسرة في قصة يحيى في هذه السورة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r4.claim: Jesus said this to them, then did not speak again until children ordinarily begin to speak.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p243#2/r4.anchor: كلمهم عيسى بهذا ثم سكت فلم يتكلم حتى بلغ المدة التي يتكلم فيها الصبيان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:30-35/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:30-35/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:30-35/r4.claim: The peace on Jesus at birth, death, and resurrection means God's protection in those stages.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:30-35/r4.anchor: والسلام علي يوم ولدت... } الآية. أي: السلامة علي من الله تعالى في هذه الأحوال.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p222#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p222#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p222#2/r6.claim: 'Peace upon me' and the birth and death phrases refer to those times, while being raised alive refers to Resurrection Day.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p222#2/r6.anchor: {والسلام علي يوم} [مريم: 33] حين. {ولدت ويوم} [مريم: 33] وحين. {أموت ويوم أبعث حيا} [مريم: 33] يوم القيامة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r2.claim: Jesus first declares himself God's servant, not a deity or part of a trinity, and a prophet; he must perform worship, was born, will die and be raised like others, and his words imply prayer existed among prophets after Abraham despite differences in form.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r2.anchor: Böylece Hz. Îsâ kendisinin bir ilâh değil bir kul ve bir peygamber olduğunu, ilâhî varlığın üç öğesinden biri olmadığını ilân etmiş oldu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r5.claim: The passage summarizes Jesus as God's servant and prophet, blessed everywhere, obligated to worship, respectful to his mother, neither tyrannical nor disobedient.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:29/r5.anchor: 30-33. âyetlerde Hz. Îsâ’nın başlıca nitelikleri şöyle sıralanmaktadır

SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r1.claim: The definite article in al-salām is anaphoric to the earlier salām on John, so that same peace is directed to Jesus.
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r1.anchor:
قوله: { والسلام }: الألف واللام فيه للعهد؛ لأنه قد تقدم لفظه في قوله:
وسلام عليه
[مريم: 15]، فهو كقوله

SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers the generic article as an insinuation of a curse on Mary's accusers: peace belongs to Jesus in particular, implying its opposite for them, as in 20:47.
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري- بعد ذكره ما قدمته -: " والصحيح أن يكون هذا التعريف تعريضا باللعنة على متهمي مريم

SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r3.claim: Yawma wulidtu is governed by the implied stability in ʿalayya; it cannot depend on al-salām because a verbal noun and its complement would be separated.
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r3.anchor: قوله: { يوم ولدت } منصوب بما تضمنه " علي " من الاستقرار. ولا يجوز نصبه ب " السلام " للفصل بين المصدر ومعموله.

SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r4.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads wulidtu as an active past verb referring to Mary, with the feminine tāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r4.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن على " ولدت " جعله فعلا ماضيا مسندا لضمير مريم، والتاء للتأنيث.

SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:33/r5.claim: Ḥayyan is an emphatic circumstantial accusative.

ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r11.claim: سلام may mean the verbal noun of سلمت and general safety, the plural of سلامة, or one of God's names.
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r11.anchor: فالسلام مصدر سلمت سلاما، ومعناه عموم العافية والسلامة، والسلام جمع سلامة، والسلام اسم من أسماء الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r12.claim: An indefinite سلام can begin a sentence because it is frequently used and generic nouns can convey nearly the benefit of definiteness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r12.anchor: وسلام مما ابتدئ به في النكرة، لأنه اسم يكثر استعماله.

ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r13.claim: Because سلام appeared earlier without the article, repeating it as السلام is better, though either form is possible.
ZAJJAJ:v3p328/r13.anchor: بغير ألف ولام كان الأحسن أن يرد ثانية بالألف واللام

ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n23/r1.claim: Though 3:46 says Jesus would speak in the cradle, verses 30–33 may use past tense as a trope to project what would become true later.
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n23/r1.anchor: verses 30-33 seem to be in the nature of a trope, projecting the shape of things to come by using, for the sake of emphasis, the past tense

ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r1.claim: Asad considers it inconceivable for divine revelation and prophethood to be granted before full intellectual and experiential maturity.
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r1.anchor: it is not conceivable that anyone could be granted divine revelation and made a prophet before attaining to full maturity of intellect and experience

ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r4.claim: Alternatively, Jesus may have spoken the whole passage after maturity, summarizing the ethical principles of his prophetic life and his awareness that he was God's servant.
ASAD-NOTES:19:27#n24/r4.anchor: the whole of this passage (verses 30-33) may also be understood as having been uttered by Jesus at a much later time

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus' peace at birth, death, and resurrection parallels John's and shows that Jesus too passed and will pass through each human life phase; weak reports cannot override this, and the Qur'an supports no contrary claim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: just as every human being passes through all these phases of life, Jesus (sws) too passed and will pass through these phases.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes al-salām as a generic article that indirectly curses Mary's accusers: if peace belongs to Jesus, its opposite is theirs, like the warning about whoever rejects guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: هذا التعريف تعريض بلعنة متهمي مريم وأعدائهما من اليهود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the definite article as referring back to the greeting given to Yahya at his three vulnerable moments.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r5.anchor: وقيل: أل لتعريف المنكر في قصة يحيى في قوله وسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r6.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads yawma wulidtu as a past-tense clause, 'the day I was born.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r6.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي يوم ولدت أي يوم ولدتني جعله ماضيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r7.claim: The author prefers the forms wa-salāmun ʿalayya and al-salāmu ʿalayya when the greeting is from God; the following wording is Jesus speaking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r7.anchor: ورجح وسلام علي والسلام لكونه من الله وهذا من قول عيسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r8.claim: Another view prefers Jesus's greeting because God made Jesus speak in His place as God's representative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p259/r8.anchor: وقيل: سلام عيسى أرجح لأنه تعالى أقامه في ذلك مقام نفسه فسلم نائبا عن الله

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.claim: In ليس غير and ليس إلا, an understood complement such as ذاك is omitted for brevity because the listener can recover it.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.claim: Arabic may omit an understood الواحد after من; Sibawayh adduces ordinary speech, Qur'an 4:159, and poetry as parallels.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.claim: In the cited poetry, expressions like من جمال and ما في قومها omit جمل and أحد, with the missing noun inferred from context.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكليسغيروليسإلاكأنهقالليس.claim: ما الدهر إلا تارتان means one of the two turns brings death and the other a hard-won life; deletion after غير is comparable to omitting the rest of a compound name.

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r1.claim: Proper names are needed to report a particular ruling about a particular individual, since specific attribution requires identifying the subject specifically.
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r1.anchor: فاحتيج إلى وضع الأعلام لهذه الحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r2.claim: People have more distinct needs tied to individual persons than other animals do, so human individuals receive proper names more often.
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r2.anchor: كانت الحاجات المختلفة تثبت لأشخاص الناس فوق ثبوتها لسائر الحيوانات

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r3.claim: Proper names divide into personal names, titles, and kunyas; examples include Ibrahim, Israel, and Abu Lahab, respectively.
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r3.anchor: العلم إما أن يكون اسما كإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أو لقبا كإسرائيل أو كنية كأبي لهب

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r4.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r4.claim: Sibawayh illustrates a name with kunya (hyena, lion, fox, scorpion), a name alone (Qutham for a male hyena), and a kunya alone (Abu Baraqish for an animal).
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r4.anchor: سيبويه أفرد أمثلة الأقسام المذكورة من تركيب الكنية والاسم وهي ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r5.claim: Kunyas may be formed by adding a reference to a father, mother, son, or daughter; examples include Abu Jaʿda, Umm Layla, Ibn Daʾya, and Bint al-Jabal.
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r5.anchor: الكنية قد تكون بالإضافات إلى الآباء وإلى الأمهات وإلى البنين وإلى البنات

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r6.claim: Kunya additions may have unknown lineage (Ibn ʿIrs) or known lineage: a camel's offspring is Ibn/Bint Makhad after a year, then Ibn/Bint Labun once its mother has given birth and has milk.
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r6.anchor: الإضافة في الكنية قد تكون مجهولة النسب نحو ابن عرس وحمار قبان وقد تكون معلومة النسب

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r7.claim: When name and title combine, an unannexed name is joined to the title as one name (Saʿid Karz); with an annexed name, the title stays separate (ʿAbd Allah Batta).
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r7.anchor: الاسم إما أن يكون مضافا أو لا فإن لم يكن مضافا أضيف الاسم إلى اللقب

RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r8.claim: Kunya motives include stating a fact, expressing hope, signaling the opposite, reciprocal naming between a famous man and father, and association with a notable trait.
RAZI-FULL:v1p44/r8.anchor: الحكم السادس : المقتضي لحصول الكنية أمور : أحدها الاخبار عن نفس الأمر

BURHAN:v2p402/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p402/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p402/r1.claim: The confirmatory circumstantial qualifier is stable rather than changing and reinforces the verb; it is confirmatory because the state is already known from its governing expression. Examples include being raised alive, acting as corrupters, smiling while laughing, and being sent as a messenger.
BURHAN:v2p402/r1.anchor: الثاني الحال المؤكدة وهي الاتية على حال واحده عكس المبينة فانها لاتكون الا منتقله وهي لتاكيد الفعل

BURHAN:v2p181/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p181/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p181/r2.claim: The source notes an inference that Jesus’ speech from قال إني عبد الله to أبعث حيا has thirty-three words, matching an inferred lifespan of thirty-three years.
BURHAN:v2p181/r2.anchor: ثلاث وثلاثون كلمة وعمره ثلاث وثلاثون سنة

BURHAN:v4p92/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p92/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p92/r1.claim: In Jesus' greeting, the definite al-salam evokes the prayer's source in God's name al-Salam; invoking a divine name exposes the speaker to what that name denotes.
BURHAN:v4p92/r1.anchor: والسلام اسم من اسمائه مشتق من السلامه

ITQAN:v3p178/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r7.claim: An emphatic circumstantial accusative is another form; examples include “alive,” “doing corruption,” “a messenger,” “turning away” and “not far away.”
ITQAN:v3p178/r7.anchor: رابعها الحال المؤكدة نحو ﴿ ويوم أبعث حيا ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.claim: Yawm can mean a time or occasion, as in the times of birth, death, resurrection, travel, residence, and harvest.
DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.anchor: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا يعني حين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.claim: The indefinite سلام signals broad, comprehensive peace, while definite السلام is specific or restricted.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.anchor: والنكرة عادة تدل على الشمول والعموم والمعرفة تدل على الإختصاص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.claim: Yahya's greeting is indefinite because it comes from God, while Isa uses the definite form when speaking of himself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.anchor: وتحية سيدنا يحيى - عليه السلام - هي من الله تعالى لذا جاءت بالتنكير (سلام عليه) أما تحية عيسى - عليه السلام - فهي من نفسه فجاءت بالمعرفة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r4.claim: He adds that Isa chose the definite form out of etiquette before God rather than greet himself with the more comprehensive indefinite form.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r4.anchor: وعيسى - عليه السلام - لم يحيي نفسه بالتنكير تأدباً أمام الله تعالى فحيّى نفسه بالسلام المعرّف

DAMGHANI:v1p150/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r7.claim: Ḥayāt can mean life after death on the Day of Resurrection; 46:33 and 75:40 also refer to God reviving the dead.
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r7.anchor: السادس : الحياة يوم القيامة قوله تعالى في سورة مريم
